# Requirements Document: Net positions, clearings and short remittances

## Introduction

On each remittance date the Clearance Manager nets every party's clearances
into one position, pays settlement payees through clearings, and collects from
remittance payers.  When a remittance payer pays short, it splits what it
received.  The sources leave open how EasyPay clearances enter the netting,
and give two different rules for splitting a short payment, so the model takes
the answers as parameters.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Accounting/Clearing.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Accounting/Clearing.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-805

**User Story:** As a Clearance Manager, I want each party's clearances netted into one amount per remittance date, so that each party makes or receives one transfer and the transfers balance.

**Rule:** WHEN the Clearance Manager nets the clearances for a remittance date THE SYSTEM SHALL make each party a settlement payee or a remittance payer for its net position. (Lean: `settlementRole`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the Clearance Manager nets the clearances for a remittance date THE SYSTEM SHALL give each party the amounts of the clearances it is paid less the amounts of those it is netted as payer of.
   - ONE-805.1, proven: proven theorem `net_position_formula`; example `settlementPlanNetting`
2. WHEN a party's net position for a remittance date is positive THE SYSTEM SHALL make it a settlement payee for that amount.
   - ONE-805.2, proven: proven theorem `positive_position_payee`; example `settlementPlanNetting`
3. WHEN a party's net position for a remittance date is negative THE SYSTEM SHALL make it a remittance payer for that amount.
   - ONE-805.3, proven: proven theorem `negative_position_payer`; example `settlementPlanNetting`
4. IF a clearance is paid through EasyPay THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL leave it out of the net position of its payer.
   - ONE-805.4, proven: proven theorem `easyPay_left_out_of_payer`; example `easyPayNetting`
5. THE SYSTEM SHALL make the net positions of all parties for a remittance date sum to zero.
   - ONE-805.5, open: open theorem `net_positions_sum_zero`; counterexample `easyPayNetting`

#### Open question on ONE-805.5

> The net positions of all parties on a remittance date sum to zero.
>
> Open question for the business.  Under the reading that leaves an EasyPay
> clearance out of its payer's position and keeps it in the payee's, the
> positions add up to the EasyPay amounts.  The example `easyPayNetting`
> shows it: a seller owing an airline 100.00 by settlement plan and 50.00 by
> EasyPay is a remittance payer for 100.00, while the airline is a settlement
> payee for 150.00.  Does the EasyPay provider count as a party in the
> netting?

### Requirement ONE-806

**User Story:** As a settlement payee, I want each clearing's total to match the bank transfer I receive, so that I can reconcile the transfer clearance by clearance.

**Rule:** WHEN the Clearance Manager sends a clearing THE SYSTEM SHALL make its total, and the bank transfer for it, the amounts settled less the amounts clawed back. (Lean: `clearingTotal`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN the Clearance Manager sends a clearing to a settlement payee THE SYSTEM SHALL make its total the amounts settled for clearances marked Fully Settled, Partially Settled or Final Settlement, less the amounts clawed back.
   - ONE-806.1, proven: proven theorem `payee_clearing_total`; example `sampleClearingTotal`
2. WHEN the Clearance Manager sends a clearing to a remittance payer THE SYSTEM SHALL list its EasyPay clearances and leave them out of the total.
   - ONE-806.2, proven: proven theorem `payer_clearing_leaves_out_easyPay`; example `payerClearingWithEasyPay`
3. THE SYSTEM SHALL never make the total of a clearing to a settlement payee negative.
   - ONE-806.3, open: open theorem `payee_clearing_nonneg`; counterexample `clawbackExceedsDue`

#### Open question on ONE-806.3

> The total of a clearing to a settlement payee is never negative.
>
> Open question for the business.  A payee whose clawbacks in a clearing exceed
> what it is due in that clearing gets a negative total, which a bank transfer to
> the payee cannot carry.  The example `clawbackExceedsDue` shows it: a
> payee due 200.00 with 300.00 clawed back has a total of minus 100.00.  Does the
> payee then become a remittance payer, or is the clawback carried forward to a
> later clearing?

### Requirement ONE-807

**User Story:** As a settlement payee, I want a short remittance split by one known rule, so that I can tell which of my clearances were settled.

**Rule:** WHEN a remittance payer pays short and the Clearance Manager has no credit line THE SYSTEM SHALL split what was paid across the payer's clearances. (Lean: `allocate`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHEN a remittance payer pays short THE SYSTEM SHALL settle no clearance for more than the payer owes on it.
   - ONE-807.1, proven: proven theorem `allocation_within_owed`; example `olderClearancesFirst`
2. WHEN a remittance payer pays short THE SYSTEM SHALL settle a clearance to a settlement payee only after every older clearance to that payee is settled in full.
   - ONE-807.2, proven: proven theorem `allocation_oldest_first_per_payee`; example `olderClearancesFirst`
3. WHERE the Clearance Manager follows the Remittance of Funds page THE SYSTEM SHALL give each settlement payee its share of the payment in proportion to what it is owed, rounded to a minor unit and capped at what it is owed.
   - ONE-807.3, proven: proven theorem `proportional_share_settled`; example `twoAirlines`
4. WHERE the Clearance Manager follows the Transfer of Funds page THE SYSTEM SHALL apply the payment to the payer's clearances in the order they were recorded, whatever the payee.
   - ONE-807.4, proven: proven theorem `transfer_oldest_first`; example `twoAirlines`
5. WHEN a remittance payer pays short THE SYSTEM SHALL allocate the whole payment and no more.
   - ONE-807.5, open: open theorem `allocation_whole_payment`; counterexample `threePayees`
6. IF a remittance payer pays short THEN THE SYSTEM SHALL settle each clearance for the same amount whichever source page the Clearance Manager follows.
   - ONE-807.6, open: open theorem `one_allocation`; counterexample `twoAirlines`

#### Open question on ONE-807.5

> A short payment is allocated in full and no more: the amounts settled add
> up to what was paid.
>
> Open question for the business.  Under the Remittance of Funds page each
> settlement payee's share has to be rounded to a minor unit, and the rounded
> shares need not add up to the payment.  The example `threePayees` shows
> it: 100.00 split between three payees owed 100.00 each settles 99.99 when
> shares are rounded down and 100.02 when they are rounded up.  Under the
> Transfer of Funds page the whole payment is allocated
> \(`transfer_allocates_all`\).  How is a proportional share rounded, and
> who receives the remainder?

#### Open question on ONE-807.6

> A short payment settles each clearance for the same amount under either
> source page.
>
> Open question for the business.  The Remittance of Funds page splits a short
> payment across the settlement payees in proportion to what each is owed; the
> Transfer of Funds page applies it to the payer's obligations in the order
> they were recorded, whatever the payee.  The example `twoAirlines` shows
> them differ: a payer owing airline A 100.00 \(older\) and airline B 100.00
> \(newer\) pays 100.00, and A and B receive 50.00 each under the first page and
> 100.00 and nothing under the second.  Which allocation does the Clearance
> Manager use?
